findings.title: Recognize storage content independently of its extension
findings.description: Manifest decoding and evidence availability are gated on a lowercase .json suffix. In an isolated committed Git fixture, deleting a gzip payload makes its .json manifest unavailable, but renaming the identical manifest to .log makes evidence_exists return true and the protected-base audit return no errors. Retrieval returns the manifest bytes as plain evidence, bypassing payload existence, integrity, ownership, revision and execution metadata checks. Recursive raw_utf8 JSON renamed .txt also passes audit. This violates the prospective fail-closed storage contract and allows an invalid compact reference to satisfy generic task or review evidence availability.
findings.requested_change: Detect storage markers independent of filename, or reject storage-shaped records under unsupported extensions, and route all availability checks through the classifier. Apply the plain JSON raw_utf8 rule to JSON content independently of extension. Preserve opaque historical evidence compatibility and add renamed/uppercase/extensionless manifest and renamed raw_utf8 negative tests.
